name: Tooling

hero.title: Catch the bug that type-checks and never updates.
hero.lede: `pyreon doctor` runs up to ten gates over your app and returns one score from 0 to 100, with the fix printed under each finding. Behind it: 133 lint rules that know what a signal is, a test kit that can assert an effect did not re-run, and a DevTools panel for the reactive graph.

why.title: Tooling that knows how Pyreon breaks.

items.title: It knows the framework
items.text: Generic linters see valid TypeScript. `pyreon/no-props-destructure` sees `({ title }) =>` and flags it: a destructured prop is read once and breaks reactive prop tracking.

items.title: A score you can gate on
items.text: `pyreon doctor --ci` exits 1 on error findings only. Warnings cost points, advisory best-practice findings never block, and a gate that scanned nothing says so instead of passing.

items.title: Findings on the exact line
items.text: `--gha` prints GitHub Actions annotations with file, line and column, so each finding sits on the diff in "Files changed".

items.title: Tests that can say "did not"
items.text: `expectEffect(e).notToReRunWhen(() => theme.set('dark'))` asserts an unrelated write left an effect alone. A render-counting test cannot express that.

before.label: ships
before.caption: Type-checks with `tsc`, compiles, renders once. When the parent changes `title`, the heading never updates.

after.label: caught
after.caption: `pyreon lint` names the line and the rule. The fix reads props where they are used and keys the list.

extraSectionsHtml:
the toolbox

Every tool, and when you'd reach for it.

pyreon doctor

Project health in one command

Gates run in parallel and isolate failures. One 0–100 score with a letter grade, a bar per category, and a fix under each finding.

$ pyreon doctor --ci --gha
pyreon check

The pre-commit scan

Runs the compiler's detectors over the files you changed since HEAD, prints each finding with its fix, and exits 1 if anything is left.

$ pyreon check
@pyreon/lint

133 rules that know the framework

Five presets, a config file with a JSON schema, watch mode, --why-off to explain a disabled rule, and an LSP server for your editor.

$ pyreon lint --watch
@pyreon/testing

Testing Library, plus the reactive graph

render, screen, fireEvent and every query as you know them, plus matchers for fire counts, effect re-runs and leaks.

expectSignal · expectEffect · expectNoReactiveLeak
@pyreon/devtools

See the reactive graph

A Chrome DevTools panel with six tabs. Click a component to highlight it on the page. Built from the repo and loaded unpacked.

Components · Graph · Signals · Effects · Profiler · Console
Ctrl+Shift+R

An overlay in every dev build

Built into the runtime, tree-shaken from production: orphan signals, the latest updates with their cause chain, and Pick to inspect bound text.

$p.reactivity() · $p.pick()
pyreon info · upgrade

Keep versions in line

info lists every installed @pyreon/* version and flags skew. upgrade aligns them to one version, as a dry run until you pass --write.

$ pyreon upgrade --write
pyreon add · new

Start and grow a project

new scaffolds a web app, or iOS and Android too with --native (experimental). add installs a package and prints how to wire it in.

$ pyreon add @pyreon/form
doctor gates

What doctor checks.

Gates that audit the Pyreon repo itself skip in your app and say why. They never count against your score.

gatecategorycatches
react-patternscorrectnessReact habits: useState, useEffect, className, React imports
pyreon-patternscorrectnessFor without by, destructured props, a signal written as a call
lintper ruleEvery configured @pyreon/lint rule
islands-auditarchitectureDuplicate, dead, nested or unregistered islands
ssg-auditarchitecture404 placement, dynamic routes without getStaticPaths, non-literal revalidate
content-auditarchitectureMissing titles, broken internal links, orphaned pages
native-auditarchitectureWeb-only imports and declarations the native build drops, in files that import @pyreon/primitives (needs @pyreon/native-compiler)
check-deduparchitectureTwo versions of one @pyreon/* package in the lockfile
dependency-fabricarchitecturePhantom deps, version drift, cycles (runs when @pyreon/loom is installed)
audit-teststestingTests that build fake vnodes instead of rendering through h()
distributionarchitecturePackage hygiene for libraries laid out like the Pyreon repo
doc-claimsdocumentationNumbers in the Pyreon docs that disagree with the source (Pyreon repo only)
audit-leak-classesbest practicesMemory-leak heuristics; advisory, never graded (Pyreon repo only)
audit-typesarchitectureTyped but never-read public fields (--full, Pyreon repo only)
bundle-budgetsperformanceGzipped entry size against locked budgets (--full, Pyreon repo only)

demo.title: Run doctor.
demo.text: A simulated run on a small app, using finding codes doctor really prints. Fix findings and watch the score move: errors cost 10 points, warnings 3, info 1, per category, and the score is the mean of the categories that were measured.
demo.referenceHtml:
~/acme-apppyreon doctor

  
findings
demo.spec: Terminal panel shows "pyreon doctor" output: score N/100 with letter grade (A ≥90, B ≥80, C ≥70, D ≥60, else F), one bar per measured category (correctness, performance, architecture, testing), the top four open findings with code and file:line, and a footer listing skipped gates with the real reasons (doc-claims and audit-leak-classes: "targets the Pyreon monorepo"; audit-types and bundle-budgets: "enable with --full"). The findings card lists seven findings; clicking one toggles it fixed. "pyreon doctor --fix" marks the auto-fixable ones (no-classname, no-signal-call-write) fixed; "reset" restores all. Category score = 100 minus the sum of penalties (error 10, warning 3, info 1), clamped to 0..100; overall = rounded mean of the four categories.

items.name: pyreon doctor
items.text: 15 gates (10 for any app), a 0–100 score with a letter grade, `--only` / `--skip` to pick gates, `--fix` for lint and React-pattern fixes.

items.name: pyreon check
items.text: scans git-changed files (or the paths you pass), prints each fix, `--json` for tools.

items.name: `pyreon-lint --why-off <rule>`
items.text: says whether a rule will run, and which config line turns it off.

items.name: Editor support
items.text: `pyreon-lint --lsp` serves diagnostics and inlay hints; a VS Code extension ships in the repo.

items.name: Parallel linting
items.text: runs of 200 files or more spread across a worker pool; results are sorted so CI diffs stay stable.

items.name: Leak matchers
items.text: `expectNoReactiveLeak` checks that mount plus unmount leaves no graph growth; `expectGarbageCollected` replaces the WeakRef dance.

items.name: DevTools panel
items.text: Components, Graph, Signals, Effects, Profiler and Console tabs, with click-to-highlight on the page.

items.name: pyreon info and upgrade
items.text: find version skew before it trips the duplicate-instance guard, then align every `@pyreon/*` dependency.

limits.title: Add --ci to gate a build
limits.text: Plain `pyreon doctor` always exits 0 so it can run as a report. `--ci` exits 1 when an error finding is left.

limits.title: check and lint are different engines
limits.text: `pyreon check` runs the compiler's detectors on changed files. The lint rules (96 on in `recommended`) run under `pyreon lint`. `pyreon doctor` runs both.

limits.title: Review --fix on React code
limits.text: The React fixes turn `useState` into `signal()`, but setter calls like `setCount(n)` stay as written. Rewrite them as `count.set(n)` before you commit.

limits.title: Compile tests the way you compile the app
limits.text: Put `@pyreon/vite-plugin` in your vitest config. Without the Pyreon compiler, `{total()}` in JSX renders once and a DOM assertion after a click fails.

limits.title: Graph matchers need a dev or test build
limits.text: Production builds drop the reactive graph, so the matchers throw a clear error there. The leak matchers also need `--expose-gc`.

limits.title: Two extensions install from the repo
limits.text: The DevTools panel is built and loaded unpacked; the VS Code extension is linked from `packages/tools/lint/vscode`. Neither is in a store yet.

comingFrom.title: No dependency arrays, so no exhaustive-deps. The rules cover what goes wrong instead.
comingFrom.note: Save it as `.pyreonlintrc.json` and run `pyreon lint --watch`. `effect()` tracks what it reads, so there is no array to keep in sync. The `app` preset turns on 95 of the 133 rules, among them destructured props, `count(x)` used as a write, `.map()` in JSX, and `window` read during SSR.

comingFrom.title: Same queries, same events. The render comes from @pyreon/testing.
comingFrom.note: The queries are re-exported from `@testing-library/dom`, the package under React Testing Library. Add `@pyreon/testing/vitest` to `setupFiles` for cleanup between tests and the jest-dom matchers.

comingFrom.title: From "what re-rendered?" to "which effect re-ran?", asserted in a test.
comingFrom.note: Components run once, so there is no render to count. In the browser, the DevTools panel's Effects and Profiler tabs and the Ctrl+Shift+R overlay show what fired and why.

recipes.title: Gate every pull request
recipes.text: One job prints annotations on the diff and fails when an error finding is left. Warnings still lower the score but do not fail the job.
recipes.code:
# .github/workflows/health.yml
name: Health
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  doctor:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      - run: bun install
      - run: bunx pyreon doctor --gha --ci

recipes.title: Block the commit, not the review
recipes.text: With no paths, `pyreon check` scans files changed since HEAD plus untracked ones and exits 1 on any finding. Silence a line you mean with `// pyreon-lint-ignore <code>`.

recipes.title: Prove a theme switch leaves the cart alone
recipes.text: Assertions on the reactive graph itself: what re-ran, and how often. Run them through `@pyreon/vite-plugin` with `@pyreon/testing/vitest` in `setupFiles`.

faq.q: Does doctor work outside the Pyreon monorepo?
faq.a: Yes. Ten gates check any app. The five that audit the Pyreon repo itself (distribution, doc-claims, audit-leak-classes, and the `--full` gates audit-types and bundle-budgets) skip in your app with the reason printed, and a category no gate measured is left out of the score rather than counted as 100.

faq.q: Will a warning fail my build?
faq.a: No. `--ci` exits 1 only when an error finding is left. Warnings and info lower the score; findings in the advisory best-practices category are shown but never graded and never fail `--ci`.

faq.q: Do I need check, lint and doctor?
faq.a: Use `pyreon check` in a pre-commit hook (changed files, compiler detectors), `pyreon lint --watch` while you write (the lint rules), and `pyreon doctor --ci` in CI (both of those plus the project gates).

faq.q: Where do I get the DevTools extension?
faq.a: Build it from the repo (`bun run --filter='@pyreon/devtools' build`), then load `packages/tools/devtools/dist/` unpacked from `chrome://extensions`. The Ctrl+Shift+R overlay needs nothing: it is in every dev build.
Vitest 5 (`^5.0.0` peer). It runs in happy-dom for structure; interaction and layout tests belong in a real browser through `@vitest/browser`.
